subject: Throughput credit schedule proposal for EdgeSense commit swap
messages:
From: Amelia Novak <amelia.novak@edgesense.io>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Cc: Dan Ross <dan.ross@edgesense.io>, procurement@edgesense.io
Date: Wed, 28 Mar 2028 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Options for mid-term add + smoothing?

Hi Priyom,

Quick one from our side as we prep the renewal: we want to add ~20 A100s into our Dedicated pool mid-term (targeting June 1). Finance is worried about the immediate step-up in monthly commitment and the associated invoices.

Can you outline options to smooth billing or provide credits if utilization/throughput doesn't match the higher commit in the first months? Scope: current commit = 50 A100-equivalent GPUs (monthly reserved pool), new target = 70 A100s.

Attached is our internal commit summary (edgesense_commit_summary.xlsx) — shows baseline utilization and seasonal demand spikes.

Key asks: 1) Is there a way to avoid a big invoice jump in month 1 after the add? 2) Can Redwood provide a temporary throughput credit (or trial) while we ramp? 3) Any changes to SLA or throughput guarantee when pool scales?

Thanks,
Amelia
Amelia Novak
Head of ML Ops | EdgeSense

From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
To: Amelia Novak <amelia.novak@edgesense.io>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 29 Mar 2028 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Options for mid-term add + smoothing?

Amelia — thanks for the clear ask and the spreadsheet. Quick summary of practical options we can offer for mid-term adds:

1) 3-month smoothing credit (front-loaded amortization)
   - Redwood applies a credit that offsets the incremental commitment cost across the next 3 billing cycles so your invoice step is reduced. Credit amount is based on the delta between your current committed spend and the pro-rated list price of the added capacity.

2) Throughput-hurdle credit (performance-contingent)
   - If the new pool's average monthly throughput (seq/sec) is below an agreed hurdle for the first N months, Redwood issues a credit equal to X% of the incremental spend. Encourages us to align on the throughput target and measurement window.

3) Higher commit discount (no smoothing)
   - If EdgeSense converts to a larger committed tier immediately (70 GPUs) we can increase the committed discount (more aggressive rate) but the invoice step happens immediately.

I'll loop in Karthik for concrete $ numbers and Grace for how credits will appear on the invoice. I'll attach a draft credit schedule and the ratecard.

Next steps: pick preferred approach and we can produce a formal amendment + PO guidance.

—Priyom
Priyom Das
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Amelia Novak <amelia.novak@edgesense.io>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 2 Apr 2028 10:15:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Options for mid-term add + smoothing?

Amelia — following up with the numbers so we can make a decision:

Assumptions:
- Current commit: 50 A100-equivalent GPUs, $280k/month committed spend (net list after current discounts).
- Proposed: +20 A100s => 70 total => incremental committed list delta = $112k/month.

Option A — 3-month smoothing credit (recommended for low-risk ramp)
- Structure: Redwood issues a credit equal to 60% of the incremental spend in month 1, 30% in month 2, 10% in month 3.
- Effective incremental net in month 1 = $112k * (1 - 0.6) = $44.8k (approx).
- Total discount impact to Redwood P&L is equivalent to ~25% of incremental spend amortized.

Option B — Throughput-hurdle credit (performance-contingent)
- Structure: Agree a hurdle (e.g., 420K seq/day aggregated across the pool). If actual throughput < hurdle, Redwood issues a credit equal to 40% of that month's incremental committed cost. Measurement window = calendar month; disputes resolved by sampling logs from Redwood Console.
- Benefit: Aligns pricing to delivered value; requires SLA measurement sign-off.

Option C — Immediate tier upgrade (no smoothing)
- Structure: Move to 70-GPU commit immediately; increase discount from current rate to a promotional 22% off list for the whole term. No credits but lower unit price long-term.

Which way would you prefer? If you want a blended option (part smoothing + part higher unit discount), we can draft that too. I cc'd Marissa for renewal playbook and any CS ramp support required.

-Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Head of Strategic Deals | Redwood Inference

From: Dan Ross <dan.ross@edgesense.io>
To: Amelia Novak <amelia.novak@edgesense.io>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 9 Apr 2028 08:44:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Options for mid-term add + smoothing?

Amelia — forwarding to procurement for clarity. A few constraints from our side:
1) Finance will accept a credit schedule only if it's amortized over at least 6 months (we don't want a back-loaded liability).
2) We need a defined fallback: if utilization exceeds projections and we see sustained throughput > 90% of the new commit for 2 consecutive months, we will be billed at the new commit without retro credits.
3) Legal wants a short addendum that clearly states measurement method (Redwood Console metrics) and dispute resolution (30-day window).

Can Redwood produce a DocuSign-ready amendment and a six-month amortization schedule? Also, can you include a sample invoice line to show how the credit will appear?

-Dan
Director, Procurement | EdgeSense

From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
To: Amelia Novak <amelia.novak@edgesense.io>, Dan Ross <dan.ross@edgesense.io>, procurement@edgesense.io
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Apr 2028 16:22:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Options for mid-term add + smoothing?

Dan / Amelia — appreciate the clarity. Per your procurement asks, Redwood can do the following (final proposal):

1) 6-month amortized smoothing credit (agreed)
   - Credit = 50% of the incremental committed spend applied to month 1, then equal installments over months 2-6 so net impact is smoothed.
   - Illustration (attached proposed_credit_schedule.pdf): month 1 incremental invoice = $56k net (post-credit), months 2-6 incremental = ~$18k/month.

2) Measurement + fallback
   - If pool sustained throughput >= 90% of agreed target for 2 consecutive months, billing moves to full incremental commit going forward and remaining credits stop. We will document measurement (Redwood Console aggregated seq/sec) and provide logs for dispute resolution (30-day window).

3) DocuSign + invoice sample
   - I attached the draft amendment and ratecard. We will produce a DocuSign link once you confirm "Accept" here and provide the billing PO number. The invoice will show a credit line item: "Mid-term smoothing credit (EdgeSense) - amortized" with monthly applied amounts.

Next steps: 1) Amelia / Dan confirm they accept the 6-month amortization + fallback, 2) provide PO number, 3) we send amendment for signature and update HubSpot (link below).
